citation: DeCesare, D., McClelland, A., & Randel, B. (2017). Impacts of the Retired Mentors for New Teachers program (REL 2017-225). Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences, National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Regional Educational Laboratory Central. Retrieved from http://ies.ed.gov/ncee/edlabs.
design: RCT; teacher/class-level random assignment within school (blocked by school + grade). Probationary (first-3-years) teachers at 11 Title I elementary schools in Aurora Public Schools, CO randomly assigned to Retired Mentors for New Teachers program (program group, n=38 teachers) vs business-as-usual 'buddy' mentoring (n=39 teachers); 77 teachers total. Two-year intervention (2013/14 + 2014/15). Outcomes: student MAP math and reading achievement, grades 1-5. Impacts estimated with a 2-level HLM (students within teachers; school fixed effects), adjusted for fall MAP pretest + student/teacher covariates.
problems: Single program arm vs single business-as-usual control (registry is_multi_arm=0). Four candidate student-achievement contrasts exist (math + reading, each at end of Year 1 [2013/14] and end of Year 2 [2014/15]). This is a TWO-YEAR intervention, so per the spec the end-of-treatment wave is Year 2 (2014/15); the two Year-2 contrasts are the primary records (is_full_sample=true, outcome_role=primary). The two Year-1 contrasts are interim waves and are included as additional records flagged outcome_role=secondary with timepoint='post Y1 (interim wave)' so the central merge can select the end-of-treatment wave. The report does not separately tag a 'headline' subject; both math and reading are co-primary research questions, but only the Year-1 math impact was statistically significant. Effect sizes: the report's 'Effect size' column (Tables 2, 3; footnote c) is the standardized mean difference = (adjusted mean difference)/(pooled SD of the outcome), and Table A5 footnote c explicitly calls this the 'Hedge's g calculation'; with analytic n>900 the small-sample J correction is negligible (J=0.9992-0.9994), so reported ES essentially equals g. I recomputed the standardizing SD as diff/ES (recovers the reported outcome SDs ~21-24, e.g. Y2 math 22.95, Y2 reading 21.21) and derived g_se = J*(impact_se/SD). Impact SEs already account for clustering of students within teachers (Tables 2/3 notes), so cluster_adjusted=true; n_clusters = number of teachers in the analytic sample (no ICC reported -- not guessed). n_t/n_c are the analytic-sample student counts (students with both fall and spring MAP scores), which match the analysis Ns stated in the Table 2/3 notes. Results were noted as somewhat sensitive to model specification (Appendix B); I report the benchmark model used in the main text.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Retired Mentors for New Teachers program (vs business-as-usual 'buddy' mentoring)
effect_sizes.test_name: NWEA Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) math, Rasch (RIT) scale score
effect_sizes.g_method: Report ES = adjusted mean diff / pooled SD of outcome = 0.061 (Table 2, fn c; report labels this 'Hedge's g'). Standardizing SD recovered = diff/ES = 1.4/0.061 = 22.95 (matches reported outcome SDs). g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1103, J = 0.999320, g = 0.999320*0.061 = 0.06096. g_se = J*(impact_se/SD) = 0.999320*(0.86/22.95) = 0.03745; g_var = g_se^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 2 (p. 7); design/Ns Table A2 (p. A-2), Figure A2 (p. A-5), model Appendix A (pp. A-8 to A-10)
effect_sizes.notes: End-of-treatment (Year 2) math impact. Diff = +1.4 RIT points favoring program, NOT statistically significant (p=.113). adjusted means/SDs from Table 2 (mean_t=program 179.7 (SD 24.22), mean_c=BAU 178.3 (SD 21.66)). n_clusters = 62 teachers in Y2 math analytic sample (30 program + 32 BAU; Figure A2). 2-level HLM (students within teachers, school dummies), fall MAP pretest + student/teacher covariates; SE adjusted for clustering of students within teachers (cluster_adjusted=true). No ICC reported.

effect_sizes.notes: End-of-treatment (Year 2) reading impact. Diff = +1.4 RIT points (text says 1.42) favoring program, NOT statistically significant (p=.078). adjusted means/SDs from Table 3 (mean_t=program 174.0 (SD 21.44), mean_c=BAU 172.6 (SD 20.73)). n_clusters = 57 teachers in Y2 reading analytic sample (28 program + 29 BAU; Figure A2). Same 2-level HLM with fall MAP pretest covariate; SE adjusted for clustering of students within teachers. No ICC reported. Reading impact was sensitive to inclusion of teacher-experience covariates (Appendix B Table B4).

effect_sizes.notes: INTERIM (Year 1) math impact -- earlier wave of the two-year intervention; the end-of-treatment wave is the Year-2 record above. Diff = +1.4 RIT points favoring program, STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT (p=.045; not significant after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, threshold .025). This is the report's only significant student-achievement finding. n_clusters = 70 teachers in Y1 math analytic sample (35 program + 35 BAU; Figure A1). Same HLM specification. Recorded as outcome_role=secondary so central logic prefers the Year-2 end-of-treatment estimate; is_full_sample=true (full Y1 randomized sample, not a subgroup).
